## Baselines
| Algorithm | Family | Time | Memory | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Floyd-cycle r-adding rho | Generic oracle | `21128` group ops at 28 bits | O(1) tokens | Captured locally with `ECDLP_BITS=28`; ratio `1.361x` to oracle rho reference. |
| Floyd-cycle r-adding rho | Generic oracle | `1418382` group ops at 40 bits | O(1) tokens | Existing local row in `results.tsv`; ratio `1.441x` to oracle rho reference. |
| BSGS, `m = ceil(sqrt(n))` | Generic oracle | `1295681` group ops at 40 bits | O(sqrt(n)) tokens | Current selected solver; ratio `1.316x` to oracle rho reference. |
| Frontier BSGS, `m = ceil(sqrt(n))` | Generic oracle | `1233594` group ops at 40 bits | O(sqrt(n)) tokens | New selected solver; interleaves baby and giant table growth after counted `m*P` setup. |
| Q-independent static width-3 table | Generic preprocessing | 32-bit `B=384` online `0.588x` rho after setup; one-shot `5.291x` rho | O(B^2) pair sums plus O(B) static logs | Many-public-key toy signal from REP-P084/REP-N100, but REP-N101 shows it is dominated by setup/memory-matched reusable BSGS. |
| Reusable BSGS, static-row setup matched | Generic preprocessing | 32-bit `B=384` comparator online `0.0657x` rho; one-shot `4.769x`; amortized `0.360x` over 16 challenges | O(312188) baby entries for the focused row | Same fixed-curve reusable-data model as REP-N101; this is the baseline future static decompositions must beat. |

## Literature map
| Topic | Closest work | Claim | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Generic lower bound | Shoup generic-group model | Any generic algorithm needs Omega(sqrt(n)) oracle queries under the model. | This implementation only optimizes constants inside the model. |
| Rho constant | Pollard rho birthday-search heuristic | Expected first collision near `sqrt(pi*n/2)` for random mappings. | Need empirical token-seed sweep for this exact r-adding walk. |
| Asymmetric prime-field Semaev bases | Amadori, Pintore, Sala, "On the discrete logarithm problem for prime-field elliptic curves" (IACR ePrint 2017/609) | Builds a random target-dependent base, partitions it into disjoint factor bases, and seeks one `S_m` dependency through a single Groebner-basis calculation. | This is the literature precursor of the proposed asymmetric high-arity Semaev/crossbred direction, so that formulation is not novel. The paper reports small prime-field experiments but leaves the polynomial-system cost unresolved and does not claim a rho-beating result; revisit only with a genuinely different solver mechanism and a complete cost path. |
| REP-N470 | Compositional multiplicative-coset factor bases `x^d=c` as a relation-density amplifier or below-rho route when served by an explicit signed-S3 pair-x table. | All public smooth `64 <= d <= 512` fibers over the generated 20/21/22-bit challenge instances for seeds `0x12345678,0x12345679,0x1234567a`; two fixed public cosets per eligible degree, equal-size low-x and hash-coordinate controls, exact signed reconstruction, and a 20-bit full-rank factor-log plus independent target-descent replay. | Added `tools/compositional_coset_factor_base_probe.py` hash `2fa8a4d02128b6f2926fc356bd7e43c81ac87229d47ee5407f6d3433bafde6c5`; immutable artifact `notes/compositional_coset_factor_base_rep_n470_20_21_22_3seed.json` hash `3419983a722a5f03798ee7fa2bfa1bee00f6480b0bf0b508d154ca6beb58f570`. All `54` candidate rows passed controls. Pair precompute was `1.0352x..76.6559x` rho in every row, candidate pair-x support differed by at most `0.36%` from its better matched control, and the maximum paired hit excess was `0.046875`. The 20-bit `d=95,c=1` replay reached rank 45 and recovered the public toy target, but its optimistic lower bound was `4.1814x` rho. | The power chain preserves a factor base and cannot itself amplify Semaev relation density.
